home-remodeling.title: Gut Renovations in Coral Ridge, FL | PGX Builders
home-remodeling.meta_description: Coral Ridge gut renovations in Fort Lauderdale: 1950s canal-front ranches rebuilt for how you live now, fully permitted. Call (786) 273-2524.
home-remodeling.h1: Coral Ridge ranches, rebuilt from the studs
home-remodeling.hero_sub: Whole-home remodels for the 1950s ranches and canal houses of Coral Ridge. Permitted at Fort Lauderdale Development Services, detailed to Broward HVHZ standards, and run by a licensed general contractor, Lic. CGC1539072.
intro_paragraphs: Coral Ridge runs from Sunrise Boulevard north to Oakland Park Boulevard, between the Middle River and the Intracoastal, and Bayview Drive splits it down the middle. East of Bayview the houses sit on canals with private dockage and open water beyond; west of it they back onto the Middle River behind the Sunrise Boulevard fixed bridge. Most went up in the 1950s and 60s, when Coral Ridge Properties sold low-slung block ranches with terrazzo floors, jalousie windows and a Florida room bolted on the back. The same stock continues north into Coral Ridge Country Club Estates. Owners rarely tear these down now. They gut them.

Permits come from the City of Fort Lauderdale's Development Services Department, filed online and reviewed by Building Services. Sitting above the city is the county's own code layer. The Broward County Board of Rules and Appeals keeps the Florida Building Code's Broward amendments, certifies the officials and inspectors assigned to your job, and settles code disputes. Being in the High-Velocity Hurricane Zone means glass, doors, and roof assemblies carry HVHZ approvals. Fort Lauderdale has no citywide architects' board for single-family homes outside its historic districts, though the gated enclaves nearby run their own association reviews on top of the city's.

PGX Builders Group brings 20-plus years of South Florida construction and 150-plus completed remodels and additions, each one permitted and inspected. On a Coral Ridge whole-home job the written scope is settled before demolition begins, a supervisor is present every working day, and terrazzo, dock, and landscaping stay shielded while the trades move through. One team owns the project from estimate through warranty. We also keep the site quiet, because in a neighborhood this tight the person you annoy is the one you meet at the club on Saturday.
home-remodeling.scope_heading: Inside a full Coral Ridge gut
home-remodeling.scope_intro: Whole-home work gets priced off a written scope, never a hunch. The list below covers what a Coral Ridge gut renovation almost always contains.

scope_items.name: Structural openings, engineered
scope_items.desc: Removing the block partitions that chopped 1950s ranches into small rooms, with engineered beams, sealed calculations, and a permit set that survives review.

scope_items.name: The systems nobody photographs
scope_items.desc: New panel and service, PVC replacing cast iron drains, fresh supply lines, and ductwork resized for a house that finally has sealed windows.

scope_items.name: HVHZ glass all around
scope_items.desc: Impact windows and sliders carrying High-Velocity Hurricane Zone approvals, installed with the anchoring and buck details Broward inspectors actually check.

scope_items.name: Roof and ceiling rework
scope_items.desc: Coordinating re-roof, insulation, and flat-to-vaulted ceiling changes so the low mid-century profile gains height inside without losing its lines outside.

scope_items.name: Finishes worth the address
scope_items.desc: Custom millwork, stone, and floors selected once and installed by trades who handle them daily, sequenced so nothing gets walked on twice.

faqs.q: Who actually issues my building permit in Coral Ridge?
faqs.a: Fort Lauderdale issues it. Development Services takes the application, Building Services reviews the plans and sends the inspectors. Behind them stands Broward County's Board of Rules and Appeals, the body that certifies those officials and keeps the county's Florida Building Code amendments current. In practice you deal with one city counter while the county shapes part of what that counter enforces. Filing, tracking, and inspection scheduling are ours, not yours.

faqs.q: Is it worth gutting a 1950s ranch instead of building new?
faqs.a: Usually, on these lots. A teardown restarts every zoning conversation, including setbacks and lot coverage that a 1956 house was allowed to ignore, and on a canal lot it can pull the seawall and flood elevation into the project. A deep remodel keeps the existing footprint and the mature landscaping while replacing structure, systems, and glass. We run that comparison honestly before you commit, and we will say so when new construction is the better answer.

faqs.q: Does the FEMA 50 percent rule apply to my canal-front house?
faqs.a: Possibly, and the time to find out is before design. Federal substantial-improvement rules weigh the cost of the work against the market value of the structure alone; pass that threshold in a mapped flood zone and the entire building has to satisfy current flood-elevation requirements. A good share of waterfront Coral Ridge sits in those zones. Since the answer changes where the money should go, we run it in week one rather than at permit submittal.

faqs.q: Do I need association approval in Bay Colony or Sunrise Intracoastal?
faqs.a: Assume anything visible gets reviewed. Bay Colony, north of Commercial Boulevard, is guard-gated with a protective homeowners association, and Sunrise Intracoastal, south of Sunrise Boulevard, is a gated association of a few hundred homes. Expect elevations, materials and roof color to be looked at, sometimes construction hours and staging too. That review runs alongside city permitting rather than replacing it, so plan for two approvals on separate clocks. We prepare the association package and give the gatehouse a crew list, because nothing stalls a Monday like an unbadged truck.

faqs.q: What should I budget for a whole-house remodel here?
faqs.a: Honestly, it depends on whether you are refreshing or rebuilding. New HVHZ glass throughout, new service and drains, and structural work all consume budget before anyone picks a tile, and selections then swing the total as hard as square footage does. We put it in writing with named allowances, so the contract price is the price you pay. PGX is a high-end builder and rarely the lowest of three bids. Better you hear it now than at contract signing.

home-remodeling.cta_sub: Bring drawings, a wish list, or nothing but complaints about the floor plan. Expect a written scope and a number you can actually plan around, in English o en español.

kitchen-remodeling.title: Coral Ridge Kitchen Remodeling, Fort Lauderdale FL | PGX
kitchen-remodeling.meta_description: Coral Ridge kitchens open up: the 1950s galley wall comes out, cabinetry and stone go in, permits handled by a licensed GC. (786) 273-2524.
kitchen-remodeling.hero_sub: Custom cabinetry, stone, and structural openings for Coral Ridge kitchens, designed around how you actually cook, permitted through Fort Lauderdale Development Services, and run by a licensed, insured general contractor with a supervisor on site.
kitchen-remodeling.local_heading: The wall between you and dinner
intro_paragraphs: The Coral Ridge kitchen was built as a back room. Coral Ridge Properties laid out these houses in the 1950s and 60s with a compact galley behind a block wall, a pass-through to the dining room if you were lucky, and a Florida room where the party actually happened. Sixty years on, the party is in the kitchen. So the work here is nearly always subtractive first: take the wall down, absorb the old utility room or breakfast nook, and give the island the space the original plan never allowed.

Kitchen permits go through Fort Lauderdale's Building Services division, and a real kitchen pulls building, electrical, plumbing, and mechanical trades into one package. Two Coral Ridge realities drive the scope. Those interior walls are usually concrete block, so an opening means an engineered beam, sealed calculations, and a structural inspection rather than a Saturday with a sledgehammer. And mid-century service was never sized for induction, a wine column, and a double oven, so a panel upgrade rides along. Add a window over the sink and you are also buying an HVHZ-approved unit.

Cabinetry sets the schedule, so we order it early and stage demolition around the delivery date rather than tearing your house open to wait. Stone gets templated after the boxes are set, appliances get confirmed by model number before rough-in, and the plumber does not guess where the pot filler goes. Every Coral Ridge kitchen runs against a scope agreed in writing, with someone supervising each day and the rest of the house sealed off behind plastic. Licensed and insured, Lic. CGC1539072, permitted and inspected without exception.
kitchen-remodeling.scope_intro: Line-itemed before demolition, not discovered during it. These are the elements Coral Ridge kitchens ask for most often once the wall comes down.

scope_items.name: Cabinetry built to order
scope_items.desc: Full-height custom boxes and doors, finished for coastal humidity, scaled to eight-foot mid-century ceilings instead of forced into stock catalog dimensions.

scope_items.name: Slab counters and islands
scope_items.desc: Quartzite, marble, or porcelain slabs cut to a field template, over island framing sized for the stone weight and a seating overhang that will not crack.

scope_items.name: Beams through block
scope_items.desc: Engineered headers and columns where a load-bearing block wall separated the kitchen from the living room, permitted, inspected, and hidden in the ceiling.

scope_items.name: Appliances where you want them
scope_items.desc: Relocated ranges, refrigeration, and hoods with new circuits, gas or LP lines, and exterior venting routed so the hood actually moves air.

scope_items.name: Light you can cook by
scope_items.desc: Layered lighting on separate controls, plus the panel and dedicated circuits a 1950s Coral Ridge house needs before any of it turns on.

faqs.q: Can that wall between my kitchen and living room come out?
faqs.a: Almost always, but not for free. In these block-built houses the wall may be carrying roof load, so a structural engineer sizes a beam and columns, the drawings get sealed, and Fort Lauderdale inspects the steel before it disappears into the ceiling. Budget for the engineering and the permit as line items, not afterthoughts. The payoff is the sightline from the front door through to the canal, which is the whole reason people buy here.

faqs.q: How long am I cooking on a hot plate?
faqs.a: Plan on months, not weeks, and most of that waiting happens before demolition. Custom cabinetry runs a long lead time, appliance packages can run longer, and we would rather your kitchen work while the shop builds. Once we start, a full kitchen with structural work and relocated plumbing typically runs a couple of months on site. We set up a temporary kitchen somewhere sensible and give you a written schedule with dates on it.

faqs.q: Is a permit really needed if nothing moves?
faqs.a: A true like-for-like swap in the same locations is limited work. But the moment plumbing shifts, circuits get added, a hood vents outside, or a wall opens, Fort Lauderdale wants a permit and inspections, and kitchens rarely stay inside that narrow lane. Unpermitted work has a habit of surfacing during a Coral Ridge closing, when a buyer's attorney finds a kitchen the city has no record of. Fixing it then costs multiples.

faqs.q: Will a modern kitchen look wrong in a mid-century ranch?
faqs.a: Not if the proportions are respected. These houses have low ceilings, long horizontal lines, and big glass, which flat-panel cabinetry, continuous counters, and a restrained palette suit better than heavy traditional millwork. The mistakes we see are vertical: towering hoods, stacked upper cabinets, and islands scaled for a two-story house. Keep the horizon low and the kitchen reads like it belongs to the architecture instead of arguing with it.

faqs.q: Which line items drive a kitchen budget here?
faqs.a: Cabinetry and stone lead, appliances follow close behind, and the invisible third is what the house needs before any of it can be installed: beams, panel capacity, new supply and drain lines, proper venting. That last category is where vague bids hide. We price it openly after measuring, with allowances tied to real products you can go look at. We are not the cheapest number you will receive, and we will not pretend otherwise.

kitchen-remodeling.cta_sub: Twenty minutes standing in the room beats any photo album. We measure, ask the awkward questions, and send back a scope you can price against, in English o en español.

bathroom-remodeling.title: Bathroom Remodeling, Coral Ridge FL Homes | PGX Builders
bathroom-remodeling.meta_description: Bathroom remodeling in Coral Ridge, Fort Lauderdale. Primary suites, frameless glass, and waterproofing flood-tested before tile. Call PGX at (786) 273-2524.
bathroom-remodeling.hero_sub: Primary suites, guest baths, and powder rooms in Coral Ridge houses, built with stone, frameless glass, and a waterproofing system that gets flood-tested before tile. Permitted through the city, inspected at every stage, supervised by a licensed general contractor.
intro_paragraphs: An original Coral Ridge house came with two bathrooms, sometimes two and a half, sized for a family that showered quickly and did not own a hair dryer. The primary bath is typically a five-by-eight box with a tub, one sink, and a window that faces the neighbor. Owners along Bayview Drive and in Coral Ridge Country Club Estates fix that by annexing a bedroom or a closet: one real primary suite with a double vanity, a walk-in shower, and a tub that is there because someone wanted it.

Bath work is permitted by the City of Fort Lauderdale, with plumbing, electrical, and mechanical inspections booked before anything gets covered. That sequence is the whole value. Inspectors carry certification from Broward County's Board of Rules and Appeals, and their visit lands while the rough plumbing and the membrane are still visible. The local wrinkle is what these houses are made of: slab-on-grade floors and original cast iron drains. Cutting a slab for a curbless pan is routine here; finding a failing stack afterward is not a good day.

Think of it as a waterproof box holding expensive things; we build it that way. The membrane is flood-tested and photographed before any tile lands, slopes get checked with a level, niches are formed inside the waterproofing rather than carved in afterward, and heavy glass hangs on blocking put there deliberately. Then the ordinary manners: dust walls, protected routes, a supervisor daily, and a written scope agreed before selections are ordered. Coral Ridge humidity punishes shortcuts, so we do not take them.
bathroom-remodeling.scope_intro: Bath scopes are settled on paper before selections are ordered. Below is what a Coral Ridge primary suite or guest bath usually involves.

scope_items.name: Annexing a bedroom
scope_items.desc: Annexing a bedroom, hall closet, or linen alcove to create a real primary suite, with framing, rough plumbing, and the permit all in one package.

scope_items.name: Curbless on a slab
scope_items.desc: Saw-cutting and recessing the slab where the structure allows, linear drains set to true slope, and pans flood-tested before a tile is placed.

scope_items.name: Cast iron retired
scope_items.desc: Replacing original drains and galvanized supply while walls and floor are open, which is the only moment this ever costs a reasonable number.

scope_items.name: Stone, glass, and hardware
scope_items.desc: Slab vanities and shower walls, heavy frameless glass on solid blocking, and coastal-rated hardware chosen to survive salt air off the Intracoastal.

scope_items.name: Exhaust that leaves the building
scope_items.desc: Exhaust sized correctly and ducted outside, moisture-rated fixtures, and light placed where people actually shave and apply makeup instead of one ceiling glare.

faqs.q: Will a curbless shower work over a mid-century slab?
faqs.a: Often, yes. The slab gets saw-cut and recessed where the structure and existing drain line permit, then the pan is formed to slope and flood-tested. Sometimes the plumbing runs the wrong direction, or a post-tension slab makes cutting unwise, and the honest alternative is a low-profile curb that reads nearly the same in the room. We look under your floor before you commit to the picture.

faqs.q: Should the old cast iron drains go while the bath is open?
faqs.a: In a house from the 1950s or 60s, the answer is usually yes. Cast iron of that vintage is at or near the end of its service life, and no one wants a new marble bath draining into a stack that is scaling shut. A camera goes down the lines early so the call rests on footage instead of opinion. Whatever needs replacing gets replaced while access is free, because doing it later means opening finished work.

faqs.q: How do inspections work on a bathroom permit in Fort Lauderdale?
faqs.a: The city inspects in stages: rough plumbing and electrical before the walls close, then a final once fixtures are set. The inspectors hold Broward County Board of Rules and Appeals certification and apply the Florida Building Code with the county's amendments on top. We book each inspection, meet the inspector on site, and file the approved plans and sign-offs in one place you can hand a buyer a decade from now.

faqs.q: Do we have to move out while the suite is torn up?
faqs.a: Most Coral Ridge clients stay put, assuming a second working bath exists. We seal a dust barrier at the suite, run a protected route from the door to the work area, and keep demolition noise inside normal hours. The underestimated part is water shut-off days and the smell of certain waterproofing and adhesives. We name those dates ahead of time so you can arrange to be somewhere else.

faqs.q: Why is one bathroom quote double another?
faqs.a: Usually because one includes the parts you cannot see. Waterproofing systems, new drains and supply, proper exhaust, blocking for glass and grab bars, and slab work all cost money and none of them photograph well. Slab stone and heavy frameless glass widen the gap further. We would rather show you the line items and let you decide what to keep than win on a number that quietly leaves the membrane out.

bathroom-remodeling.cta_heading: Pick the bath that annoys you
bathroom-remodeling.cta_sub: Send photos or show us in person. Back comes a scope, a schedule, and a price we will stand behind, in English o en español.

home-additions.title: Home Additions in Coral Ridge, Fort Lauderdale FL | PGX
home-additions.meta_description: Coral Ridge additions in Fort Lauderdale: push out back, go up a floor, or convert the garage. Setbacks and engineering handled. (786) 273-2524.
home-additions.h1: Room to grow on a 1950s lot
home-additions.hero_sub: Rear extensions, upper floors, garage conversions, and in-law suites for Coral Ridge houses. Zoning checked, structure engineered, permits pulled at Fort Lauderdale, and daily site supervision from a licensed and insured general contractor.
home-additions.local_heading: Going up when out is taken
intro_paragraphs: Coral Ridge lots were platted for one-story living, and on a canal the back yard is spoken for by a dock, a pool, and a setback. That is why so many additions here go up rather than out. A second story over an existing ranch on Bayview Drive buys bedrooms and a water view at once. Off the water, in Imperial Point or Coral Ridge Isles, the more common moves are a rear family room, a garage converted into a real suite, or a wing added for parents who came south permanently.

Additions live or die in Fort Lauderdale's Unified Land Development Regulations before they ever reach the Building Services counter. Setbacks, lot coverage, and height for your residential district decide the envelope; where the plan needs relief, the city's Board of Adjustment hears the variance, which adds months. Waterfront lots bring in the federal substantial-improvement threshold, since a large addition to a house in a mapped flood zone can trigger compliance for the whole structure. New openings need High-Velocity Hurricane Zone approvals, and removing a protected tree takes its own city permit.

Foundations, tie-beams, and the joint between old structure and new are the invisible half of an addition, and handling them is where a general contractor earns the fee. We run the engineer, tie new footings into existing block correctly, and blend stucco texture and roof plane so nobody's eye stops at the seam. The house stays livable through most of the work, the site gets swept every evening, and a single team carries the job from feasibility sketch to certificate of occupancy.
home-additions.scope_heading: How a Coral Ridge house gains space
home-additions.scope_intro: Each begins with a zoning check and a structural opinion, because the envelope and the footings decide what is possible long before the drawings look pretty.

scope_items.name: Second story over block
scope_items.desc: Evaluating existing walls and footings first, then designing an upper floor with new columns, tie-beams, and a stair that does not eat the living room.

scope_items.name: Rear extension to the setback
scope_items.desc: Family rooms and primary suites pushed back as far as the rear setback and lot coverage allow, with new footings and roof tie-ins engineered together.

scope_items.name: Garage into living space
scope_items.desc: Converting the carport or garage into conditioned rooms with insulation, HVHZ openings and permitted mechanical work, so the space is legal square footage.

scope_items.name: Guest and in-law suites
scope_items.desc: Independent suites with a bath, sitting room, and kitchenette, planned to satisfy code and zoning rather than to become an unpermitted second dwelling.

scope_items.name: Footings, steel, and seams
scope_items.desc: Underpinning, new foundations, and the stucco, roof, and finish transitions that decide whether an addition reads as original or as an obvious afterthought.

faqs.q: How much bigger can I actually build on my Coral Ridge lot?
faqs.a: Your zoning district answers that before an architect does. Fort Lauderdale's land development regulations set front, side, and rear setbacks, maximum lot coverage, and height limits, and on a canal lot the rear setback is often the binding constraint. We pull the property record and run the envelope at the start, so the first sketch you see is one that can be built. If the plan needs relief, we tell you the Board of Adjustment route and what it costs in time.

faqs.q: Will my 1950s block house hold a second floor?
faqs.a: Frequently yes, sometimes with reinforcement, and only an engineer settles it. The existing walls and footings get assessed, and where they come up short the design adds columns, deeper footings, or a rebuilt tie-beam. We have also told clients outright that a rear extension buys more usable space for less money than going vertical. You get options with numbers attached, not one plan presented as destiny.

faqs.q: Does an addition put my whole house into flood compliance?
faqs.a: It can, on lots inside mapped flood zones, which includes a lot of waterfront Coral Ridge. The federal substantial-improvement rule measures the cost of the work against the market value of the structure, and crossing the threshold means the entire building must meet current flood requirements, not just the new part. That reshapes both the design and the budget. It is a week-one analysis for us, because finding out at permitting is how projects get shelved.

faqs.q: There is a big tree where the addition wants to go. Now what?
faqs.a: You will need a city tree removal permit, and replacement planting or a payment in lieu is typically part of the approval. Sometimes the cheaper and better answer is to move the footprint eight feet and keep the canopy, which on these lots also keeps the afternoon shade you will miss in August. We look at the tree during the first site visit and design around it when the geometry cooperates.

faqs.q: From first meeting to finished room, how long?
faqs.a: Think in quarters, not weeks. Design and structural engineering take time, city plan review takes more, and an addition needing a variance adds a hearing calendar on top. Construction itself commonly runs several months, longer for a second story with a new roof. A realistic frame for a substantial Coral Ridge addition is roughly a year from first conversation to furniture, and we put the phases in writing so nothing is a mystery.

home-additions.cta_heading: Test the idea before you draw
home-additions.cta_sub: Send the address and the wish list. We check the envelope, read the feasibility straight, and come back with numbers that are not wishful, in English o en español.

outdoor-living.title: Terraces & Summer Kitchens, Coral Ridge FL | PGX Builders
outdoor-living.meta_description: Outdoor living in Coral Ridge, Fort Lauderdale. Summer kitchens, pool terraces, pergolas, and impact openings on ocean-access canals. Call (786) 273-2524.
outdoor-living.h1: The yard is the other living room
outdoor-living.hero_sub: Terraces, summer kitchens, pergolas, driveways, and new impact openings for Coral Ridge homes. Detailed for coastal wind and salt air, permitted through Fort Lauderdale, and built by a licensed and insured general contractor.
outdoor-living.local_heading: Where the boat is the view
intro_paragraphs: In Coral Ridge the backyard usually ends at a seawall, and whatever sits between the house and the water gets used year round. East of Bayview Drive the canals run deep with no fixed bridges to the inlet, so the terrace competes for attention with a boat. What owners build is an outdoor room with a purpose: a covered summer kitchen that works when it rains, a shaded seating area that survives August, a pool deck detailed for bare feet, and lighting that makes the dock look intentional after dark.

Exterior work in Coral Ridge involves more agencies than people expect. Structures, utilities and paving go through the City of Fort Lauderdale, and any roofed terrace or pergola is designed against High-Velocity Hurricane Zone wind loads. Anything in the water is a separate conversation: docks, lifts and seawalls need a license from Broward County's Aquatic and Wetland Resources Program alongside the city permit, and the city regulates how far a dock and a moored vessel may project into the canal. New and substantially improved seawalls now carry a minimum top elevation of five feet NAVD88, matching Broward County's countywide standard.

Outside gets the same standard as inside. The gas, water, and power feeding a summer kitchen are permitted and inspected rather than buried and hoped over. Pergola footings are engineered and anchored. Decks pitch water away from the slab, and any metal, fastener, or cabinet within reach of Intracoastal air is specified for that exposure, because salt locates the cheapest component in a single season. The job runs on a written scope, with a supervisor here daily and the site left clean each evening, gates and neighbors included.
outdoor-living.scope_intro: One terrace or the whole stretch between house and seawall, every element below is drawn, permitted, and built under a single contract and a single schedule.

scope_items.name: Summer kitchens that are plumbed
scope_items.desc: Gas, water, and power run to the terrace under permit, marine-grade stainless and cabinetry, and counter material picked to take sun, rain, and canal air.

scope_items.name: Shade that is engineered
scope_items.desc: Roofed outdoor rooms, trellises, and pergolas on designed footings with connections detailed for hurricane uplift, proportioned to the long low rooflines already here.

scope_items.name: Pool decks and drainage
scope_items.desc: Pavers, shell stone, or finished concrete laid to slope water away from the house, with the grading and drainage sorted before anything is set.

scope_items.name: Driveway, walks, and stucco
scope_items.desc: Cracked mid-century driveways and paths replaced with material and geometry that fix the arrival, plus exterior stucco repair and a paint scheme worth choosing.

scope_items.name: Impact doors to the terrace
scope_items.desc: Swapping tired sliders for HVHZ-approved impact units that open the house to the water properly and pass inspection on the first visit.

faqs.q: Do you handle the dock and seawall too?
faqs.a: We build what sits on land and coordinate what sits in the water. Docks, lifts, and seawalls are marine trades with their own licensing, and they usually need a Broward County Aquatic and Wetland Resources license on top of the city permit. We bring in a marine contractor and sequence their work with ours, so nobody pours a terrace the week a barge needs the seawall. One schedule covers both, and you still have a single point of contact.

faqs.q: My seawall is old. Does replacing it change what I can build behind it?
faqs.a: Often, yes. Fort Lauderdale now regulates seawalls as tidal flood barriers with minimum top elevations, and repairing beyond a certain share of a wall pulls the whole thing up to the current standard. A raised cap changes grades, which changes how the terrace, steps, and drainage behind it have to work. If a seawall is anywhere on your horizon, sequence it before the hardscape rather than after, and we will plan the elevations together.

faqs.q: What keeps a canal-side outdoor kitchen from rusting away?
faqs.a: Specify for the environment once instead of replacing it twice. Marine-grade stainless, powder coating over the right substrate, sealed dense stone, and hardware rated for coastal exposure all cost more up front and simply last. Big-box outdoor cabinetry near the Intracoastal tends to look sad within a couple of seasons. We also detail the counter and cabinet layout so rain drains out of the boxes rather than sitting in them.

faqs.q: Is a pergola or covered terrace really a permitted structure?
faqs.a: Yes. Anything roofed or anchored to the ground takes a building permit, engineered footings, and connection details reviewed against High-Velocity Hurricane Zone wind loads, since Broward sits inside the HVHZ. That review separates a shade structure from a projectile. Electrical, gas, and plumbing feeding it carry their own trade permits and inspections. Drawings, submittal, and the inspection calendar are part of what you hire us for.

faqs.q: What moves the price on a backyard project?
faqs.a: Roof and utilities, mostly. A paver terrace and a covered outdoor room with gas, water, power, and a full appliance package are different projects wearing similar photographs. Grading and drainage can also be a bigger line than expected on flat lots near the water. Pricing follows a site walk and a measured plan, with allowances pinned to named products, so what you compare is a real scope instead of a number per square foot.

outdoor-living.cta_sub: Walk us out back and describe the evenings you want. A written scope and a real schedule follow, in English o en español.

permitting-compliance.title: Permits, Inspections & Closeout in Coral Ridge FL | PGX
permitting-compliance.meta_description: Coral Ridge permits handled through Fort Lauderdale: open records closed out, HVHZ approvals, inspections and condo repair work. Call (786) 273-2524.
permitting-compliance.h1: Legal on paper, not just built
permitting-compliance.hero_sub: We file the permits, document the product approvals, meet the inspectors, and clear the old records a title search turns up. Coral Ridge houses, canal lots and condo units, all of it under one general contractor's license, CGC1539072.
intro_paragraphs: Two kinds of people call about permits here. The first is planning a real project and wants it filed properly from day one. The second already has the problem. A lender pulls the record on a Bermuda Riviera ranch and finds a reroof from 2003 with no final inspection. A Florida room off Bayview Drive was closed in and air-conditioned by an owner three deeds back. Jalousies became sliders in Coral Ridge Isles one summer, unpermitted. A lift went in behind a Sunrise Intracoastal house because the barge arrived and the paperwork never did.

Coral Ridge is inside Fort Lauderdale city limits, so the file opens at the Development Services Department, goes to its Building Services Division for review, and moves through the LauderBuild portal. Broward then adds its own layer on top: the county Board of Rules and Appeals maintains the local amendments to the Florida Building Code, certifies the plans examiners and inspectors assigned to your job, and issues the interpretations that settle disputes. Nothing in the building envelope clears review without approval documentation valid in the High-Velocity Hurricane Zone, installation details included. Bay Colony and Sunrise Intracoastal add association review on a separate clock.

PGX Builders Group is a licensed general contractor, not a permit expediting service, so the name on the application is the name that answers for the work. Where a submittal needs an architect, an engineer or a surveyor, we bring one in and coordinate the set. Plan review comments get answered once, properly, instead of bouncing back three times. A supervisor is on site when the inspector arrives. Across more than twenty years here and 150-plus remodels and additions, all of them permitted and inspected, the expensive failures we have watched people inherit were almost never structural. They were clerical, and they waited.
permitting-compliance.scope_heading: Permit work on a Coral Ridge address
permitting-compliance.scope_intro: Some of this gets filed before a shovel moves. The rest gets untangled years later, usually under a deadline. Either way it is the same five jobs.

scope_items.name: Old records, finally closed
scope_items.desc: The city keeps a history for every address. We read yours, work out what each dormant permit is still short of, and take it through inspection, revision or replacement.

scope_items.name: Florida rooms and carports
scope_items.desc: The enclosures, garage conversions and added baths that never saw a permit, brought onto the record with as-built drawings, engineering where structure is involved, and inspection.

scope_items.name: Product approvals for the HVHZ
scope_items.desc: Every opening and roof assembly carries a current product approval into review, matched to the design pressures for that wall rather than a generic sheet.

scope_items.name: Inspections nobody has to repeat
scope_items.desc: We call each phase when the work is genuinely ready and meet the inspector on site, because a second visit costs a week and every trade queued behind it.

scope_items.name: Condo repairs after the report
scope_items.desc: Concrete restoration, waterproofing, balconies and railings for buildings along the Galt Ocean Mile, permitted, inspected and sequenced so residents keep their elevators and their parking.

faqs.q: The title search found a permit from 2003 that was never closed. What now?
faqs.a: First we read the file, because open is not one condition. Some permits are short only the final inspection nobody ever called. Some need a revision, or a sealed letter from the engineer of record. Some cover work that changed after approval. Then there is the version where no permit exists at all and one has to be obtained after the fact. Every path ends with an inspector looking at something, so start as soon as you know.

faqs.q: Is there a county approval on top of the Fort Lauderdale permit?
faqs.a: None that you file. Every residential permit here is reviewed, issued and inspected by Fort Lauderdale, with the submittal going up on LauderBuild. Broward's Board of Rules and Appeals sits a level above that, writing the amendments your plans examiner applies and certifying the people who apply them, which is where the county's consistency comes from. The county office you may actually deal with is environmental licensing, and it attaches to anything built in or over a canal.

faqs.q: Our Florida room was enclosed decades ago with no permit. Does it have to be fixed?
faqs.a: Not today, and nobody is coming to look. It turns into a problem when someone else reads the record: a buyer's inspector, a lender's appraiser, an underwriter who notices conditioned square footage the city has never heard of. Legalizing it means as-built drawings, an engineer weighing in on what holds the roof up, and a permit measured against today's code rather than the code of the year somebody swung the hammer. Sometimes that is painless. Sometimes the old glass has to come out.

faqs.q: Our Galt Ocean Mile building just got its milestone report. Can PGX do the repairs?
faqs.a: Yes. The signature on that report belongs to an engineer or architect the association hires, and we are not it. Milestone inspections and structural integrity reserve studies apply to condominium and cooperative buildings of three habitable stories and up, which describes most of the towers here and at Coral Ridge Towers. Broward County layers its own Building Safety Inspection Program on top, enforced through the city's building official and exempting one- and two-family homes. We build the repair list, permitted and inspected.

faqs.q: What does permitting add to the schedule and the budget?
faqs.a: On the schedule, think weeks rather than days, with the first submittal setting the pace. A complete set draws one round of comments; a rushed one draws three, and each round restarts the wait. A bathroom that stays inside its own walls moves fastest. Sealed engineering, flood compliance or anything touching the canal runs longer, because those reviews happen one after another. Fees are the city's, not ours, and they track the declared value of the work.

permitting-compliance.cta_sub: Send the address and the closing date, if there is one. You get the permit history and a written scope for clearing it, in English o en español.
